record.paper_title: Convolutions in geometric function theory: Recent results and open problems.
record.context_brief: Hadamard convolution and the class DCP
record.original_question: Let S be the class of analytic univalent functions on the unit disk D = {z : |z| < 1} that are normalized by g(z) = z + ⋯. For each direction ψ, let C_ψ be the subclass of S consisting of functions that are convex in the direction ψ. Define DCP to be the family of analytic functions f on the unit disk such that, for every ψ ∈ [-π, π] and every g ∈ C_ψ, the Hadamard convolution f * g belongs to C_ψ. Is the truncated exponential polynomial ∑_{k=0}^{n} (1+z)^k / k! contained in DCP for general n? The source notes that this has been verified for n ≤ 20.

evidence.quote: Let C_{\psi} denote the subset of functions f\in S=\{g: g(z)=z+..\). analytic univalent in D=\{| z| <1\}\} that are convex in the direction \psi. Then the class DCP is the family \{ f: f analytic in U, f*g\in C_{\psi} for all \psi\in [-\pi,\pi] and all g\in C_{\psi}\}.
He asks, for example, whether \sum^{n}_{k=0}(1+z)^ k/k!\in DCP\; this is true for n\leq 20.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $S$ be the class of analytic univalent functions $g$ on $\mathbb{D}$ normalized by $g(z)=z+a_2z^2+a_3z^3+\cdots$. For $\psi\in[-\pi,\pi]$, a function $g\in S$ is said to be convex in the direction $\psi$ if its image $g(\mathbb{D})$ has the property that, for every $w_0\in\mathbb{C}$, the intersection of $g(\mathbb{D})$ with the line $\{w_0+te^{i\psi}:t\in\mathbb{R}\}$ is connected (possibly empty). Let $C_\psi\subset S$ denote the subclass of functions convex in the direction $\psi$. The Hadamard convolution of two analytic functions $f(z)=\sum_{k\ge 0}a_kz^k$ and $g(z)=\sum_{k\ge 0}b_kz^k$ on $\mathbb{D}$ is defined by $(f*g)(z)=\sum_{k\ge 0}a_kb_kz^k$. Define the class
$$\mathrm{DCP}=\{f\text{ analytic on }\mathbb{D}:\,f*g\in C_\psi\text{ for every }\psi\in[-\pi,\pi]\text{ and every }g\in C_\psi\}.$$
For every positive integer $n$, determine whether the truncated exponential polynomial
$$P_n(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{(1+z)^k}{k!}$$
belongs to $\mathrm{DCP}$.

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any publication explicitly resolving whether the truncated exponential polynomials $\sum_{k=0}^n (1+z)^k/k!$ lie in the class DCP for all $n$. Related literature on convolution-preservation of convexity-in-one-direction (Ruscheweyh–Sheil-Small style results) was found, but no definitive resolution of this specific question was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Harmonic Mappings Convex in One or Every Direction
status_evidence.snippet: Studies functions convex in a given direction and convolution preservation, but does not address the truncated exponential polynomial DCP question.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on convolution and convexity in a direction does not address the specific question.

status_evidence.title: Convolution properties of univalent harmonic mappings convex in one direction
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses convolution of mappings convex in one direction.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution found of whether the truncated exponential polynomials belong to DCP for all n.
